mathematics.assertion_tested: Exact finite root-to-C2-unit-character correspondence, quotient-ring evaluation laws, reduction naturality, complete finite reduction forests, terminal-depth stable cores, and explicit failures of automatic lifting or universal plus/minus-one classification.

bounds.coefficient_map_naturality: Every high/low depth pair, every root at the high depth, both C2 values, all 25 coefficient probes.
bounds.finite_lift_forests: Every edge between consecutive levels; compare direct terminal projections with independent backward pruning.
bounds.nonreduced_evaluation_pairs: Every ordered pair of quotient elements over each F2[epsilon]/epsilon^r, for r=2,3,4.
bounds.nonreduced_naturality: All roots, all coefficient pairs and all length-reducing quotient maps including augmentation to F2.
bounds.quotient_ring_evaluation_pairs: Every pair of quotient elements when modulus <=16; otherwise every ordered pair from coefficient probes (a,b) with a,b in [-2,2].
bounds.root_and_unit_character_enumeration: Every residue at every declared prime-power level.
specific_boundaries: 3 mod 8 has no root lift mod 16
plus/minus-one collision mod 2 but separation mod 4
extra dyadic roots at tested depths >=3 have no next-level root lift
nonreduced characteristic-two rings have roots besides plus/minus one

mathematics.coefficient_domain: Z/(p^m), exact integer residue arithmetic; F2[epsilon]/(epsilon^r), exact bit-vector coefficient arithmetic.
mathematics.conventions: C2 is {0,1} with addition modulo 2. Character generator value is x; identity value is one. R[X]/(X^2-1) elements have coefficient order (1,X). Depth zero is the zero ring. Binary bit i is the epsilon^i coefficient. Each reduction forest stops at its explicitly declared terminal depth.
non_claims: No universal theorem or infinite-branch classification follows from this finite run.
No arithmetic Galois-group construction, Hodge-Tate comparison, Weil-Deligne attachment, or completed full partial claim is asserted.
Finite stable cores mean extension only to the declared terminal level.
No novelty claim or external mathematical result is required.
